title: Ratatouille
subtitle: Provençal slow-cooked vegetable stew
excerpt: The sun-drenched vegetable stew of Provence: aubergine, courgette, peppers, and tomatoes cooked long and slow in olive oil with garlic and thyme until everything is soft, silky, and deeply flavoured. Better the next day; good warm or at room temperature.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ratatouille is the great vegetable stew of Provence, taking its name from the French ratouiller, meaning to stir up. The dish uses the summer vegetables of the Mediterranean: aubergine, courgette, peppers, tomatoes, onion, and garlic, all of which ripen at the same time. There are two main approaches: the classical method, which cooks all the vegetables together in a single pot from the start (quicker, rougher in texture); and the Escoffier-influenced method, which cooks each vegetable separately to preserve its distinct character before combining. The classic method is closer to the home cooking tradition of Nice and Marseille; the separate-cooking method is the restaurant approach. Both are valid. The version here uses the classical approach, which is simpler and produces a more unified, unctuous result. True ratatouille is not a quick dish: the vegetables need time in the pot to collapse and meld.

content.text: Salt the aubergine and courgette before cooking to draw out moisture; this stops them steaming and going watery in the pot. Use a wide, shallow pan so the vegetables can cook in a single layer as much as possible. Do not rush: the finished stew should be very soft, almost melting, with no resistance to the bite.

content.text: Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large wide pan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the red peppers and cook for 5 minutes. Add the aubergine and courgette and stir to combine. Add the remaining oil.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, oregano, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Stir well. Cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Remove the lid and cook for a further 20 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are very soft and the stew is thick with no excess liquid. Remove the bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Scatter with parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature. Excellent the next day.
